description: Managed infrastructure services proposal for a multi-site precision manufacturing group.
provenance: Modeled on enterprise managed-services proposals following infrastructure discovery: current-state risk, target operating model, service levels, cost baseline, transition waves, governance, pricing, and decision path. Deliberately exercises a nine-slide deck with a five-year run-cost chart, operational KPI cards, and detailed contractual terms.

document.presentationTitle: Managed Infrastructure Services Proposal — Calder Precision Group

content.title: Managed Infrastructure Services Proposal
content.subtitle: Prepared for Calder Precision Group | August 26, 2026 | Proposal NB-26417 | Valid through October 10, 2026

content.title: Standardize 14 plants and lower five-year run cost by $12.7M.
content.subtitle: Executive proposition
prose: Scope covers service desk, endpoint, network, server, cloud, and backup for 5,840 users.
Delivery spans 14 plants in the United States, Mexico, and Germany.
Calder retains production authority through its seven-person OT engineering team.

content.title: Discovery findings — cost and resilience gaps
content.subtitle: Six-week assessment completed with IT, plant engineering, finance, and security
bulletPoints: Four service desks use different tools and priority definitions; first-contact resolution ranges from 31% to 68% by region
1,126 endpoints are beyond manufacturer support and 14% of Windows devices miss the 30-day critical-patch standard
Plant network outages caused 47 hours of production interruption in FY2025, with estimated contribution loss of $3.8M
Backup jobs succeed 96.7%, but only 62% of tier-one systems have a tested recovery procedure within the past year
Infrastructure labor includes 38 contractors at blended rates 22% above the regional market median
Monitoring generates 18,400 monthly alerts; 74% close without action and obscure a recurring storage-capacity issue

content.title: Current model versus proposed operating model
content.subtitle: What changes after the 24-week transition

content.title: Committed service outcomes by month nine
content.subtitle: Measured monthly and subject to service credits

content.title: The managed model lowers cost while funding modernization
content.subtitle: Five-year infrastructure run cost, $M; excludes application development and OT engineering

content.title: Transition plan — control before transformation
content.subtitle: Twenty-four weeks from contract signature to steady-state acceptance
bulletPoints: Weeks 1-4 — mobilize governance, confirm asset baseline, validate security access, and freeze critical runbooks
Weeks 5-9 — transfer service desk and endpoint operations; shadow all production incidents before ownership changes
Weeks 10-14 — transition server, cloud, backup, and network operations in paired regional waves
Weeks 15-19 — deploy event correlation, patch rings, and the unified configuration management database
Weeks 20-24 — prove service levels, complete two recovery exercises, and secure Calder acceptance
No involuntary Calder employee transfer assumed; NexBridge will offer roles to 11 identified contractors

content.title: Commercial terms
content.subtitle: Five-year managed-services agreement; all figures USD
bulletPoints: Recurring managed-services fee — $18.6M in Year 1, indexed at the lower of 3% or CPI thereafter
Transition and tooling — $2.4M fixed fee, payable against four accepted milestones
Included volume bands — 5,500-6,250 users, 14 plants, 620 servers, and 410 network devices
Service credits — up to 12% of monthly charges; chronic failure creates termination rights after cure
Productivity commitment — 4% annual unit-cost reduction for eligible service towers beginning Year 3
Exit assistance — up to nine months at contracted rates with full asset, runbook, and data handover

content.title: Decide by October 10 to preserve the January transition.
content.subtitle: Recommended next steps
prose: September 9: plant-manager service review; September 16: commercial redlines.
